extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners before the USPTO; OED/disciplinary staff and counsel handling reciprocal discipline
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and procedural criteria for imposing reciprocal discipline on a registered patent practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24, including the special three-part test for applying discipline nunc pro tunc and notice/publication requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline procedure under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director may file a Complaint for Reciprocal Discipline requesting that the Director of the USPTO impose reciprocal discipline identical to that imposed by another jurisdiction; a Notice and Order is mailed (certified mail) and delivered to the respondent and provides an opportunity to file within forty (40) days a response opposing the imposition of reciprocal discipline based on one or more of the reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the respondent fails to file a response, the Office may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose the reciprocal discipline. The Notice should be served (example: certified mail) and state the complaint for reciprocal discipline; the respondent has 40 days to respond opposing on the statutory grounds. Authority cited: 35 U.S.C. §§ 2(b)(2)(D) and 32; 37 C.F.R. §§ 11.19 and 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treating a state suspension on ethical grounds as a USPTO rule violation (37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)(i))
rubrics_metrics.description: A license to practice law in a state that has been suspended on ethical grounds may constitute a violation of USPTO professional conduct rules (here cited as 37 C.F.R. § 10.23(b)(6) via § 10.23(c)(5)(i)), supporting reciprocal suspension before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office will identify the underlying ethical findings in the foreign disciplinary order (examples here: attempting to charge an unreasonable fee in violation of Illinois Rules 8.4(a)(1) and 1.5(a); conduct involving dishonesty, fraud, deceit or misrepresentation in violation of Rule 8.4(a)(4); conduct tending to defeat the administration of justice or bringing the profession into disrepute in violation of Illinois Supreme Court Rule 770). Those findings can be the factual/legal basis for a USPTO suspension.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirements to obtain reciprocal discipline nunc pro tunc (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: Reciprocal discipline may be imposed nunc pro tunc upon request by a practitioner only if the practitioner: (1) promptly notified the OED Director of his or her suspension or disciplinary disqualification in another jurisdiction; (2) establishes by clear and convincing evidence that the practitioner voluntarily ceased all activities related to practice before the Office; and (3) complied with all provisions of § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The effective date of reciprocal discipline applied nunc pro tunc is the date the practitioner voluntarily ceased practice-related activities before the Office and complied with § 11.58. Evidence may include a dated letter to the OED Director (example: letter dated October 10, 2011 notifying the OED Director), Office records supporting the asserted cessation date (example: cessation on October 31, 2009), and a statement of compliance (or prompt compliance upon receipt of final order) with § 11.58. The Office requires clear and convincing evidence for the voluntary cessation claim.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compliance with 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 as a condition for nunc pro tunc relief
rubrics_metrics.description: One of the prerequisites for applying reciprocal discipline nunc pro tunc is compliance with all provisions of 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 (the regulation referenced for post-discipline obligations).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Practitioner must have complied with (or commit to immediate compliance upon issuance of the Final Order) any duties in § 11.58 (e.g., duties related to termination or suspension of practice before the Office). The Final Order may condition nunc pro tunc effectiveness on such compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents and publication of Notice of Suspension (Official Gazette and Reading Room posting)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director shall publish notice of suspension (example text provided) in the Official Gazette and make disciplinary decisions available for public reading in the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Published notice should identify the respondent (name, residence, registration number), specify the nature and basis of the suspension (statutory/regulatory violations, underlying jurisdictional discipline and reasons), state the effective date (including nunc pro tunc date if applicable), and cite the statutory/regulatory authority for the action. The Office will post the disciplinary decision on its Reading Room web page (example link provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Notice to other jurisdictions and courts under 37 C.F.R. § 11.59
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the respondent is admitted, to courts where the respondent is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This notice obligation ensures other licensing authorities and courts are informed of USPTO discipline; the Final Order directs the OED Director to carry out those notifications in addition to publication in the Official Gazette.

rubrics_metrics.name: Restitution/reimbursement obligations arising from underlying discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: Where the underlying jurisdiction's discipline included reimbursement (example: the Supreme Court of Illinois ordered that respondent reimburse the Client Protection Program Trust Fund for any Client Protection payments arising from his conduct), that factual/legal consequence is referenced in the USPTO proceeding and may form part of the public notice of discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The USPTO decision may recite and rely upon restitution or reimbursement obligations imposed by the other jurisdiction as part of the disciplinary record; such obligations may be noted in the notice of suspension even if enforcement of those specific monetary obligations is governed by the other jurisdiction.
